certification_and_marking.standard_type: Product Specification (Wood Panels & Fire Safety Materials)
certification_and_marking.certification_status: Strict Statutory Mandatory Certification. Under the statutory 'Plywood and Wooden Flush Door Shutters (Quality Control) Order' (QCO) issued by the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, Government of India, all Fire Retardant Plywood must conform to IS 5509 and bear the mandatory BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark). Manufacturing, importing, distributing, or stocking non-certified fire-retardant plywood is a criminal offense under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016. Micro and small units are granted specific delayed implementation schedules, and export-only shipments are exempt. Precious metal hallmarking is completely inapplicable to processed wood panel products.

requirements.detail: Every fire-retardant plywood sheet must carry the BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark) marked legibly, accompanied by the manufacturer's registered licence number (CM/L) and standard designation (IS 5509).

In cases where fire-retardant chemical treatment is applied at the veneer stage and finally after the manufacture of the plywood, the plywood so produced must conform strictly to the BWR (Boiling Water Resistant) grade of IS 303.

requirements.requirement_type: Permitted Methods of Fire Retardant Treatment
requirements.detail: Chemical treatment may be executed either by pressure impregnation after manufacture or by soaking of plywood/veneer. If veneer treatment is chosen, it must be performed using the soaking method.
Thickness deviations of the finished panels must satisfy strict limits: a) Less than 6 mm allows ±10 percent; b) 6 mm and above allows ±5 percent.

The straightness of edges and ends of plywood must be verified against a straight edge of at least the full length of the panel. The maximum gap (convex or concave) must not exceed 2 mm per 1 000 mm (0.2 percent).
requirements.clause_reference: Table 1, Sl No. iv & Annex A, Clause A-1

requirements.detail: Squareness of the plywood must be checked with a 1 200 mm × 1 200 mm square by applying one arm of the square to the plywood edge and measuring the maximum gap, which must not exceed 2 mm per 1 000 mm (0.2 percent).
requirements.clause_reference: Table 1, Sl No. v & Annex A, Clause A-2

requirements.detail: To retard rapid combustion, the panel must undergo standard flammability evaluations. The time taken for the second ignition of the specimen under standard flame exposure must be at least 30 minutes.
To slow thermal breakthrough, the flame penetration time through the panel thickness must be not less than 15 minutes for every 6 mm of thickness.
The time taken to lose weight from 30 percent to 70 percent under standard burning exposure must be not less than 20 minutes.
The finished plywood must be reasonably clean to handle and completely free of dirt and stains, other than a uniform surface color resulting from the flame-retardant chemical solution.
Lot grouping and statistical sampling must be drawn randomly in accordance with the specifications of IS 7638.

plain_language_summary.summary: IS 5509 : 2021 is the mandatory national Indian Standard specification establishing physical, chemical, and fire safety requirements for Fire Retardant Plywood. Under India's statutory Plywood Quality Control Order (QCO), all fire-retardant plywood sheets manufactured, imported, or sold in India must carry the Bureau of Indian Standards Standard Mark (ISI Mark). It outlines strict manufacturing methods (soaking or pressure impregnation of veneers or finished boards with flame-retardant chemicals) and mandates that plywood treated at the veneer stage must meet BWR moisture-proof grades of IS 303. To protect human life in high-risk zones (such as commercial kitchens, high-rise apartments, and public auditoriums), it enforces rigorous fire tests—demanding a minimum flammability ignition resistance of 30 minutes, a flame penetration delay of at least 15 minutes per 6 mm thickness, and a minimum rate of burning of 20 minutes to slow the spread of flames and buy critical evacuation time.
